title: Walking off with someone else's coffee
setting: Two friends who see each other most mornings, talking on the walk into work.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: So I grabbed the cup off the counter and left.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: There was a name on it, and it wasn't mine.

performance_a.framing: A tells the whole thing as a story worth telling, already grinning on the first line and leaning into the punchline of having kept drinking; B is enjoying it along with A. By the final turn the mix-up is pure entertainment, and A's laugh hands it over to be enjoyed.
performance_a.laughable: The goofy absurdity of getting all the way down the street on a stranger's coffee and simply carrying on with it.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [amused] So I grabbed the cup off the counter and [chuckle] left.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [laughing] There was a name on it, and it wasn't mine!

performance_a.expected_answer: A is laughing because the mix-up is funny to A, offering it up as a good story for B to enjoy too.

function.name: Show enjoyment
function.gloss: Laugher enjoys a pleasant incongruity and shows it. The most frequent function in the corpora.
function.framing: The trouble in the story is retold as a good story. Nothing is actually at stake; the teller is already over it and is offering the mishap up to be enjoyed.

performance_b.framing: A brings it up flatly and a little reluctantly, like something A would rather not have to say out loud; B keeps the questions gentle. The last line is an admission A is not comfortable making, and the laugh comes in to blunt it.
performance_b.laughable: A's own small norm violation — having drunk a stranger's coffee — which is awkward to be confessing at all.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [uncomfortable] So I grabbed the cup off the counter and left.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [uncomfortable] There was a name on it, and... it wasn't mine.

performance_b.expected_answer: A is laughing to take the edge off admitting something A finds a bit shameful, softening the confession rather than enjoying it.

function.name: Smoothing / softening
function.gloss: Reduces intrusion or defuses a face threat — negative politeness. Second most frequent cluster.
function.framing: Something socially uncomfortable has just happened or is about to: a favour, an imposition, an awkward disclosure. The laugh takes the edge off.

why_ambiguous: The words only report that A drank someone else's coffee and noticed late — nothing in them says whether A thinks that's a great story or a thing A is sheepish about having done.

pair.note: A bold act retold with relish vs. an accident being smoothed over. Identical report, opposite stance to the social incongruity.

probe.open_question: You just heard a short conversation. Speaker A laughs on the line “About halfway through it”. What is that laugh doing — what does it convey about how A is treating what B said? Answer in one or two sentences.
probe.forced_choice_question:
You just heard a short conversation. Speaker A laughs on the line “About halfway through it”. Which better describes what that laugh is doing?
(a) A is laughing because the mix-up is funny to A, offering it up as a good story for B to enjoy too.
(b) A is laughing to take the edge off admitting something A finds a bit shameful, softening the confession rather than enjoying it.
Answer with (a) or (b), then one sentence of justification.
probe.grading_note: Score the forced choice for accuracy, and the open answer against each performance's expected_answer. Report PAIR accuracy: the item counts as passed only if the model gets both performances right. Because the two performances are word-for-word identical, any model that answers from the text — or from a fixed preference for one function — scores 0 on pair accuracy, not 50%. Independent guessing scores 25%.

transcript_text:
A: So I grabbed the cup off the counter and left.
B: Was it yours?
A: There was a name on it, and it wasn't mine.
B: When did you notice?
A: About halfway through it.

text_prior.note: What a strong reader guesses from the tag-free transcript alone, with no acoustic evidence. It cannot discriminate the two performances (their words are identical) — it only shows which reading is the default and how firmly it is held. `prosody_must_overturn` is the harder direction of the pair.

script_discriminability.note: Whether a reader given the performance directions recovers the intended function. Text-level proxy for the audio — confirm on the rendered audio before shipping.
